analysis.title: Equities lose momentum as Iran risks keep oil volatile
key_insights: Equity rebound attempt faded on Thursday despite Anthropic's IPO debut. The listing did not ease concerns over AI investment profitability and tech sector risks.
Oil stayed volatile, rising on Thursday but below $95/bbl. Traders weighed improving supply prospects against geopolitical risk.
The US has not ruled out further military action against Iran. Tehran struck Kuwait and Bahrain on Wednesday and continued attacks on vessels trying to transit the Strait of Hormuz.
The 10-year Bund yield moved back above 3.40% and the 2-year Schatz yield rose above 3.15% as EUR rates rebounded with oil.
Markets price almost two full 25bp ECB hikes by March 2027, in line with Natixis's forecast, with some probability of a third hike next year.
The 10-year OAT-Bund spread widened by more than 3 bps to 153 bps and the BTP-Bund spread widened by 1 bp to 107 bps. OATs are the most sensitive to the broader market environment.
The dollar paused its rally, closing slightly lower at 103.8 and supported by expectations of further Fed rate hikes.
EUR/USD held at 1.0980. AUD/USD fell toward 0.667 after weak Australian October employment data and falling iron ore prices.
European indices posted a fourth straight daily decline, with the SXXP down about 0.9%. Indices reversed lower at the US open. All SXXP sectors fell except tech.
AMD fell as much as 11% early in the US session on concerns over its cross-investments with Nvidia.
The SPX posted its sixth consecutive daily decline, the longest streak since April 2024. The VIX was stable at 24 at the close of the European session.
Euro corporate primary market subscription levels improved. Boston Scientific priced a €4.25bn six-tranche deal, with the 2-, 4- and 8-year tranches about 3x oversubscribed.
Credit indices tightened on Thursday: Main by 0.3bps and Crossover by 2.7bps. CDX IG widened by 2bp. CDS on Oracle (-4bps), SpaceX (-3bps) and Meta (-3bps) narrowed after Anthropic's IPO.
Trump, Xi and Putin held trilateral talks in Shenzhen and agreed a symbolic declaration on peace and nuclear disarmament, with no concrete commitments or timelines on Ukraine or Iran.

ECB officials signalled vigilance on inflation and no sign yet of second-round effects. Nagel did not rule out another hike, Moulin called oil-driven inflation too high, and Kocher said further hikes may be needed.
Japan October core inflation rose to 2.2% y/y from 2.1% in September on higher energy prices, above the BOJ's 2% target for a second month.
UniCredit finalized an agreement with the German government on its acquisition of Commerzbank, a credit positive. The merged entity stays listed with headquarters in Frankfurt.
Tereos's credit story deteriorated after H1 results. The EBITDA guidance cut could push year-end leverage to about 10x versus 6.0x under previous guidance.
Moody's revised Toyota's outlook to Positive, citing a forecast EBITDA margin of 9.6%. Moody's and S&P reviewed Lufthansa after its TAP minority stake and kept a Stable outlook.
